title: Grid Debugging and Best Practices knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Grid Debugging and Best Practices”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Using browser grid overlays” under “Grid Debugging and Best Practices”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with grid debugging and best practices?
options: Choose grid tracks that can grow or shrink with content, and verify placement at narrow widths.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Choose grid tracks that can grow or shrink with content, and verify placement at narrow widths.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Choose grid tracks that can grow or shrink with content, and verify placement at narrow widths. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Grid Debugging and Best Practices” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
